findings.statement: Run run:5ce89f521e5e is a bounded replay of 50,000 events: 3 of 3 jobs completed, clink exit status 0, not cancelled. Thresholds: at least 5 distinct senders in a 3,600,000 ms event-time window for fan-in; onward links have a gap of at most 1,800,000 ms. The dataset holds 50,000 transfers, 12,072 accounts, 12,321 devices, 691 onward links and 6 fan-in alerts. Everything below holds only for this dataset as this run processed it.

Alert fan_in:A-37573:1794823200000: account A-37573, window 1794823200000 to 1794826800000, 7 senders, 7 transfers, total 379,500 minor units. Contributing transfers: T003057, T003091, T003124, T003154, T003248, T003287, T003319. All 7 start candidate onward-transfer paths. The longest has 4 onward links. Path accounts are A-37573, A-38045, A-93288, A-63022 and A-54215. Every path ends at A-54215, where no further qualifying transfer exists in this dataset. There are two parallel sequences of the same four hops: T003168>T003182>T003201>T003222 and T003391>T003416>T003433>T003454. All eight of those hops were sent from device D-45880. That device was used by four of the five path accounts (A-37573, A-38045, A-93288, A-63022) and by no other account in the dataset.

Alert fan_in:A-83577:1795057200000: account A-83577, window 1795057200000 to 1795060800000, 8 senders, 8 transfers, total 174,500. Contributing transfers: T022417, T022437, T022451, T022478, T022495, T022519, T022542, T022561. All 8 lead into a single sequence, T022572>T022592>T022609>T022629>T022649. That gives a longest path of 5 onward links, the deepest of the six alerts. Path accounts are A-83577, A-56768, A-83094, A-43725, A-14799 and A-39382. Paths end at A-39382, where no further qualifying transfer exists. Device D-40018 sent T022609 (from A-83094) and T022649 (from A-14799). These two path accounts are not adjacent on the path. The other hops were sent from different devices. D-40018 was also used once by A-34114, an account not on this route (T038409, later in the dataset).

Alert fan_in:A-10859:1794924000000: account A-10859, window 1794924000000 to 1794927600000, 6 senders, 6 transfers, total 204,000. Contributing transfers: T011431, T011465, T011494, T011536, T011572, T011610. All 6 start paths, and the longest has 3 onward links. Path accounts are A-10859, A-78340, A-75793, A-92332 and A-85287. The paths branch at A-78340 and end at two accounts, A-92332 (via T011600>T011628) and A-85287 (via T011695). Device D-79802 sent the debits from A-10859 (T011583, T011670) and from A-78340 (T011600, T011695). No other account in the dataset used it. The hop from A-75793 (T011628) used a different device.

Alert fan_in:A-20636:1795190400000: account A-20636, window 1795190400000 to 1795194000000, 6 senders, 6 transfers, total 36,000. Contributing transfers: T033316, T033368, T033403, T033439, T033474, T033495. Five of them link to one debit, T033506, which paid A-36729, where the paths end. That is 1 onward link at most. T033316 has no onward link. No device was used to send by two or more of its path accounts (A-20636, A-36729).

Alert fan_in:A-85921:1794855600000: account A-85921, window 1794855600000 to 1794859200000, 6 senders, 6 transfers, total 15,000. All six credits were 2,500. Contributing transfers: T005750, T005789, T005830, T005868, T005934, T005978. Four of them link to one debit, T005888, which paid A-10758, where the paths end. That is 1 onward link at most. T005934 and T005978 have no onward link. No device was shared among its path accounts (A-85921, A-10758).

Alert fan_in:A-28137:1795003200000: account A-28137, window 1795003200000 to 1795006800000, 7 senders, 7 transfers, total 29,500. Contributing transfers: T018004, T018035, T018065, T018090, T018160, T018198, T018248. None of the seven has an onward link, so the alert starts no candidate onward-transfer path. Its only path account is A-28137 itself, and no device is shared on its route.

All six alerts look alike as indicators: 6 to 8 distinct senders, one transfer per sender, in one event-time hour. They differ in recorded relationships. (a) Onward-link depth: 0 for A-28137, 1 for A-20636 and A-85921, 3 for A-10859, 4 for A-37573, 5 for A-83577. (b) Devices shared among path accounts: none for A-28137, A-20636 and A-85921. D-79802 is shared by 2 path accounts of A-10859, D-45880 by 4 path accounts of A-37573, and D-40018 by 2 path accounts of A-83577. (c) Totals: the three multi-hop alerts total 174,500 to 379,500, while the other three total 15,000 to 36,000. None of the accounts where paths end has a fan-in alert of its own. By the recorded relationships alone, A-37573, A-83577 and A-10859 show multi-hop timing sequences plus shared devices. A-20636 and A-85921 show a single onward debit, and A-28137 shows inbound fan-in only. That is a difference in recorded structure, not a determination of fraud.
Traceable provenance: each finding traces back to specific transfer ids, onward-link pairs (credit, debit) and indicator ids in this run's stored evidence, all listed in the claims.

hypotheses.statement: In alert A-37573, a single device (D-45880) sent every hop across four accounts, twice in parallel sequences, with each debit slightly smaller than the one before. This could fit one operator controlling several accounts that forward collected funds (mule-style layering). The data records only timing and device use, not ownership or fund movement.

Alerts A-83577 and A-10859 could reflect similar coordinated layering. In A-83577 the shared device appears at non-adjacent hops (A-83094, A-14799), and in A-10859 at the first two hops. Either could also be coincidental or a legitimate shared device.

Alerts A-28137, A-20636 and A-85921 involve small amounts, at most one onward link and no shared devices. They may be benign fan-in, such as collections, splitting bills or uniform small payments (A-85921: six payments of 2,500). The data does not establish this.

unresolved.question: Who owns or controls the accounts sharing devices D-45880, D-79802 and D-40018? Shared device use does not establish identity, and this dataset holds no ownership data.
What happens at the end accounts (A-54215, A-39382, A-92332, A-85287, A-36729, A-10758) beyond this bounded replay? Paths end only because no further qualifying transfer exists in this dataset.
Is the use of D-40018 by A-34114 (T038409) related to the A-83577 route in any way? The data records only the shared device, not why it was shared.
Did the onward debits draw on the credits they are linked to? Onward links record only timing, so the data cannot answer this.
